name: Zheng-Dao Heavy Industries AMR-14 'Earthquake'
description:
A bolt-action anti-materiel rifle chambered in 20mm, firing explosive-incendiary rounds designed to destroy vehicles, equipment, and light structures at ranges exceeding 2 kilometers. The AMR-14 weighs 25 kilograms and requires a bipod or fixed mounting for accurate fire — this is not a weapon that can be fired from the shoulder. Each round carries enough explosive filler to detonate a vehicle's fuel system, penetrate 30mm of armor plate, or blow a hole through a concrete wall large enough to put a fist through.

Zheng-Dao manufactures the Earthquake for military customers who need to destroy hard targets at extreme range without deploying crew-served weapons or calling for air support. A single operator with an AMR-14 can disable vehicles, destroy communications equipment, detonate ammunition stores, and render defensive positions untenable from a distance where the target cannot effectively respond with small arms. The weapon's report is catastrophic — the 20mm round produces a shockwave that shatters windows within 10 meters of the firing position and announces the shooter's location to everything within a kilometer.

The Earthquake has appeared in GLMZ's inter-corporate conflicts in roles its designers never intended. During the Tier 3 corridor wars, both sides used AMR-14s to fire through building walls at targets in adjacent structures — the 20mm explosive round penetrating exterior walls, interior walls, and anyone in between. The weapon turned entire buildings into kill zones, as occupants discovered that their walls provided no protection against a round designed to destroy vehicles.
legality: Military only — prohibited for corporate security
specifications: caliber: 20x102mm action: Bolt-action magazine: 5 rounds effective range: 2,000+ meters muzzle velocity: 820 m/s penetration: 30mm RHA at 500 meters weight: 25 kg length: 1,800mm recoil: Hydraulic buffer system
tactical_use: Extreme-range anti-materiel engagement. Operators target vehicles, generators, communication arrays, defensive positions, and personnel behind hard cover. The explosive-incendiary round ensures that hits on equipment result in destruction, not damage. Requires spotter support for engagements beyond 1,000 meters.
cultural_context: The Earthquake represents the upper limit of what a single person can carry and fire. In GLMZ's arms culture, owning an AMR-14 is a statement that you're prepared for war — not street violence, not self-defense, but war. The weapon has no civilian application and no plausible self-defense justification. Its presence means someone has decided that buildings need to be destroyed.
known_users: At least two known mercenary crews operating heavy weapons
story_hooks: An AMR-14 round punched through a corporate executive's office window from 1,800 meters — passing through the exterior wall, three interior partitions, and the executive's desk chair. The executive wasn't in the chair. The shot was a warning. The next one won't be.

Someone has been firing AMR-14 rounds into the foundations of a residential tower in the lower tiers. Structural engineers estimate that three more hits in the right locations will cause a partial collapse affecting 200 residents. No demands have been made.

physical_description.visual_profile: A massive, purpose-built anti-materiel platform resembling a portable artillery piece more than a rifle. Angular and brutal, with a pronounced muzzle brake, thick free-floated barrel, and skeletal stock. Designed for destruction at distance, not ergonomics.
physical_description.dimensions: 1,800mm length overall; 680mm barrel length; 320mm width at receiver; 280mm height with hydraulic buffer assembly
physical_description.weight_description: Brutally heavy — 25 kilograms of concentrated devastation. Requires bipod mounting or fixed rest; shoulder-firing is impossible. Feels anchored, immovable, engineered to absorb and redirect catastrophic recoil.
physical_description.primary_material: Forged steel receiver and barrel; carbon-composite stock and handguard; steel bipod with spring-loaded lock mechanism; reinforced polymer magazine housing
physical_description.finish: Matte industrial black with brushed steel breech components. Heavy wear and oxidation visible on exposed metal surfaces — this is a working weapon, not a showpiece. Hydraulic fluid staining around buffer assembly.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal black primary with steel-gray barrel and breech; burnt copper accent on the hydraulic cylinder; safety lever in industrial orange
physical_description.grip_texture: Rough-textured black polymer on the charging handle and magazine well; bare serrated steel on the bolt knob; textured polymer foregrip designed for gloved hands only
distinctive_features: Massive 20mm muzzle brake with four-chamber porting design — looks like a mini furnace
Hydraulic recoil buffer visible as a thick brushed-steel cylinder integrated into the stock
Free-floated barrel with cooling vanes machined into the profile
Integrated bipod with heavy-duty locking mechanism and rubber pads
Magazine well showing multiple 20mm round profiles; rounds visibly larger than standard rifle cartridges
Threaded muzzle with permanent muzzle brake welded in place
Charging handle resembling a miniature pry bar — over-engineered for armor-plate manipulation
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: ZHENG-DAO HEAVY INDUSTRIES cast into the left side of the receiver in industrial sans-serif; model designation 'AMR-14' stamped in white paint on the stock; serial number engraved on the breech block; small Zheng-Dao corporate logo (interlocking geometric shapes) on the mag well
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-worn but maintained. Aluminum oxide scoring on the barrel from sand/dust environment exposure. Light scoring on the stock from bipod wear and hard case storage. Hydraulic buffer assembly shows minor cosmetic corrosion. Breach lugs show subtle wear marks from hundreds of bolt cycles. This is a weapon that has been fired — often.
